beats.say: You'd need cement and steel to stop a river. A Chola king used only stones. Two thousand years later, it still works. How?
This is Kallanai, on the Kaveri near Trichy. Built by King Karikala Chola, around the second century.
beats.credit: Photo: Beckamrajeev, CC BY-SA 3.0, Wikimedia Commons

beats.say: 329 metres लंबा, और एक भी पत्थर तराशा नहीं गया।
beats.cap: 329 metres long. And not one stone was cut to shape.

beats.say: The trick? Huge uncut boulders, sunk straight into the sandy riverbed, in running water.
lines: sunk into the riverbed, in running water
beats.credit: Photo: Ashwin Kumar, CC BY-SA 2.0, Wikimedia Commons

beats.say: It splits the Kaveri into four streams, and fed sixty-nine thousand acres of farms.
Centuries later, British engineer Arthur Cotton studied it, and learned how to build on sand.
lines: Arthur Cotton learned to build on sand

beats.say: सोचो, जो सिखाने आए थे, वो यहाँ से सीखकर गए।
beats.cap: Think about it. They came to teach, and left having learned.

beats.say: By the 1900s, it watered about ten lakh acres. India's oldest dam still in use.
lines: India's oldest dam still in use

beats.say: Send this to the engineer friend who thinks old means weak. One Indian marvel every week. Follow for number three.
